central_claim: APA (Adversary Preferences Alignment) achieves significantly better black-box transferability (up to 77.48% avg ASR across 10 models) while maintaining high visual consistency compared to existing unrestricted adversarial attack methods like ACA.
claim_evidence: Abstract states 'APA achieves significantly better attack transferability while maintaining high visual consistency.' Table 1 shows APA-GC achieves 77.48% average black-box ASR vs ACA's 56.90% against normally trained CNNs and ViTs.
mre_config: Smallest MRE: (1) Train LoRA adapters on 5 images from images_un/ using visual_alignment.py (200 epochs each); (2) Run APA-SG or APA-GC attack on same 5 images using ResNet50 as surrogate model via attack_alignment.py; (3) Evaluate attack success rate on 1-2 target models (e.g., MobileNetV2, Inception-v3). This tests the core claim with minimal compute.

code_available.evidence: GitHub repo deep-kaixun/APA verified at https://github.com/deep-kaixun/APA contains complete code: attack_alignment.py (11267 bytes, attack effectiveness alignment), visual_alignment.py (9289 bytes, LoRA visual consistency alignment), pipe_ours.py (32755 bytes, AttackPipeline implementation), utils.py (5984 bytes, model loaders and augmentation), data.json (image metadata with 100 ImageNet samples), images_un/ folder with sample images, and README with documented run commands.

dataset_available.evidence: GitHub repo contains data.json metadata for 100 images from ImageNet-compatible dataset (standard benchmark from ImageNet validation set). README states 'We provide subset in images_un' and full data link to https://github.com/VL-Group/Natural-Color-Fool/releases/download/data/images.zip. images_un/ folder contains sample PNG images verified via GitHub API.

weights_available.evidence: Base models verified: Stable Diffusion v1.5 from HuggingFace (https://huggingface.co/runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5), ResNet50 and MobileNetV2 weights downloadable via model_ckpt/download.sh from PyTorch model zoo. No custom LoRA checkpoints needed for inference-only MRE.

dataset_is_standard.evidence: ImageNet-compatible dataset is a widely recognized public ML benchmark from ImageNet validation set (1000 images with class labels), commonly used for adversarial attack evaluation as cited in the paper.

agent_task: Run MRE reproduction: (1) Install dependencies (pytorch>=2.1.0, diffusers, peft, transformers, accelerate); (2) Download base models: SDv1.5 from HuggingFace (runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5), ResNet50 and MobileNetV2 weights via model_ckpt/download.sh; (3) Run attack with pre-trained diffusion model (no LoRA training needed for MRE): python attack_alignment.py --gradient_back skip-gradient --test_sample_num 5 --source_model ResNet50 --use_lora False; (4) Check attack_success_rate in output CSV to verify >50% black-box ASR against target models.

h100_estimate.basis: MRE compute breakdown: (1) Attack optimization only (no LoRA training for inference MRE): 5 images × 10 iterations × 50-step DDIM denoising × ~3-5 min each ≈ 5-7 hours on A100; (2) The diffusion model (SDv1.5 UNet + VAE + text encoder) requires ~24GB VRAM for attack computation, memory-bound on smaller GPUs; (3) Using A100 baseline at 0.32x H100 ratio: wallclock_hours * h100_equivalent_multiplier = 57 * 0.32 = 18.24 H100-hours, rounded to 18. Engineering/debugging time (diffusers version compatibility, memory optimization, model loading) adds significant overhead not included in compute estimate.

match_target.config: APA-SG attack (LoRA visual alignment stage included, as in the paper), SDv1.5 + ResNet-50 substitute model, 5 samples (MRE), skip-gradient
match_target.value: >50% black-box ASR (paper Table 1, RN-50 substitute, APA-SG: 89.0 on MobileNetV2 and 83.4 on Inception-v3; APA-GC: 97.6 and 93.5)
match_target.scope: transfer to MobileNetV2 and Inception-v3 targets with the ResNet-50 substitute
